newsitem.title: FRANCE: All who want will be in EMU by 2002 - ex BOF member.
newsitem.headline: All who want will be in EMU by 2002 - ex BOF member.

text.p: Former Bank of France monetary policy council member Jean Boissonnat said on Wednesday all EU countries which have committed themselves to European monetary union would be a part of the single euro currency by 2002.

"There will not be a single European with a euro in his pocket without the Italians, Spanish, Portuguese and others having the euro in their pocket too," Boissonnat, recently replaced on the central bank's council, told Europe 1 radio.

He also said he expected France and Germany to have public deficits this year of around three percent of gross domestic product and that he believed they would not be prevented from launching Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) on time in January 1999 even if those deficits came in at 3.1 percent of GDP.
"My personal conviction is that the Germans and the French will be ready for the euro, that is that they will have public deficits of around three percent (of GDP)," he said on Europe 1 radio.
"And if it's 3.1 percent, no one will ask them to give up because they are a tenth of a (percentage) point above what is in the (Maastricht) treaty," he said.

Asked about Italian and Spanish membership of EMU, he said the euro would probably be launched by Germany, France and a few others at the start of 1999 but that all those who wanted to join would be there by 2002, when euro notes and coins are due to go into circulation.
"What counts is that they will be there the day that all Europeans will have the new currency in their pocket, in 2002. Between 1999 and 2002 there will be a transition," he said.
"France and Germany and some others will start it off but we will all be there...the day the (EU) people will have access to (euro) coins and notes, and that's 2002," he said.
